answer: The trellis protocol makes every agent post a small time-locked deposit at registration in the raven registry, refunded only after each honest epoch of verified work, so a sybil attacker must lock fresh capital in every fake mesa identity and loses stake whenever a clone cheats or idles during an epoch. Sustaining thousands of fake identities means capital frozen forever plus steady slashing losses, which quickly exceeds any payoff from forged votes, while honest agents simply get deposits back, making identity cheap for the honest and costly to sustain for the fraudulent.
